claims.text: The live archer AI firing rule and the global projectile gravity constant are both held, closing the ledger's 'arrow arc physics' item outright. Projectile.GRAVITY = 3 (px/frame^2), applied as velY += GRAVITY every update. EnemyArcher.fireArrow() fires from (mcs.x, mcs.y-60) at a target sampled at (target.mcs.x, target.mcs.y-60), solving a fixed-45-degree-ish ballistic: velA = sqrt(GRAVITY*|dx|/0.866), velXa = velA*0.866, t = |dx|/velXa, velYa = (dy - 0.5*GRAVITY*t*t)/t, sign-flipped when firing left, then a uniform aim jitter velYa += Math.random()*8 - 4. Above level 50 a coin flip sets Damage.LAUNCH_KNOCKDOWN on the arrow. EnemyGoblinThrower uses the identical solve; EnemyKanjiGuardian divides by 0.866/3 for a flatter arc.

claims.text: The 63x72 map bitmap and the 12-bit territory-ID space ARE reconciled, exactly, and the transform is entirely in the payload. The game's own decryptor is in the repo: ResourceManager.decryptByteArray XORs bytes 3..255 with key = resourceFileNameArray[num].charCodeAt(1) AND swaps ba[i] with ba[i+256] whenever i%11==0. Applying it to all five Mobile_*Resource.bin files yields valid SWFs. 122_Mobile_SoundResource inflates to 29,623 bytes holding 13 DefineSound tags (deflect, die1, die2, die3, slash1, slash2, slash3, punch, hitmetal, fart, goodkoto, sumo, refund) and 113_Mobile_MusicResource inflates to 1,402,677 bytes holding 13 DefineSound music stems (bgm_lose, safepercussion, safekoto, safeambience, bgm_levelup, bgm_gangnam, flutes, dungeonpiano, dungeonpercussion, dungeonflute, dungeonambience, battledrums, battlechants) — all MP3, 11025 Hz, 16-bit, mono. These are byte-exact original assets, not characterisations from a YouTube rip. A plain whole-file XOR fails 68 bytes into the deflate stream, which is why every prior pass concluded 'unopenable'; the i%11 byte-swap is the missing step.

claims.lane_impact: L-combat-core: weakens (without killing) the 300/200/100-as-base arithmetic, and tells the port to derive reach from the SPD/DAN formula rather than from the 200 constant.
claims.text: InputManager.maxDistance = 200 is a compile-time initialiser, not a gameplay base. setStance calls InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength) on every battle init for the local player (web §1t99s0§.as:3156-3158, android MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094), so the 200 is overwritten before the player ever draws a stroke. Any derivation of the wiki's 300/200/100 that treats 200 as 'the shipped default slash budget' rests on a value the player never plays at. The real base is 120 + floor((90 + 5*DAN) * SPD / (20 + SPD)) — 124 at SPD 1 / dan 0, asymptotically 210 at dan 0.

claims.ledger_text: c-2 stage-px conversion: 'at 1920x1080 then converted at /1.875'
claims.text: EVERY 'stage px' NUMBER IN docs/research/fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md THAT WAS CONVERTED AT /1.875 IS 20% TOO LARGE. The correct 1080p divisor is 2.25. The web build's letterbox routine sets base 800x480 and, for a viewport wider than 800/480 = 1.6667, takes the fit-height branch: scale = stageHeight/480 and offsetX = (stageWidth - 800*scale)/2. At 1920x1080 that is scale 2.25 with 60 px pillarbox bars. Three independent confirmations: (1) source, §1t1540s0§.as:271-307 plus §1t1523s0§.as:104/106 (stageWidth 800, stageHeight 480); (2) frames -- I measured the pillarbox on four session11 frames (first/last column with any pixel >12): damage-ttk/t125.350.png 54->1862, gap-focus-trigger/t1747.000.png 48->1867, stance-reach/B_t783.400_LIGHT_stroke-anchored-at-body_farGap436px.png 52->1868, stance-reach/A_t117.400_BALANCED_lvl1_stroke235px.png 54->1863, i.e. content ~1810-1820 px = 800x2.25 = 1800 plus compression bleed, whereas /1.875 demands 210 px black bars that are simply not present; (3) reductio -- the HUD reload bar sits at row y=1036 (I measured it), which at /1.875 maps to stage y ~504, off the bottom of a 480-tall stage, physically impossible, while at /2.25 it maps to stage y ~460 of 480, i.e. the bottom HUD strip. Corrected c-2 reach bands: LIGHT 233-241 -> 194-201 (max 303 -> 252); BALANCED 116-131 -> 97-109; HEAVY 97-103 -> 81-86 (max 121 -> 101). Note the corrected Heavy MAX of 101 now kisses the source's hard 100-px floor, and every band sits at or below its source cap, which is what a body-to-endpoint distance should do against a path-length budget.
